Sourcing and landed cost · September 8, 2026 · 7 min read

What US buyers should know about 2026 import duty on plastic drinkware

Duty on plastic tableware is not one number. It is a base rate plus trade-action layers plus fees, and the classification you choose changes which layers apply.

Duty is a stack, not a rate

When a supplier quotes you "the tariff", they are usually quoting one layer. In reality a US entry can carry four separate charges on the same customs value: the ordinary most-favoured-nation rate from the product's own subheading, a Section 301 trade-action rate from Chapter 99, and then two fees — the merchandise processing fee and, on ocean freight, the harbour maintenance fee.

For plastic household and tableware articles under heading 3924 the ordinary rate is 3.4%. The trade-action layer is what people mean when they say "the China tariff", and crucially it is additive: the schedule reads "the duty provided in the applicable subheading plus 25%", not "25% instead of". You keep the base rate and gain another.

Newer trade actions have added further layers. A separate Section 301 action covering forced labour took effect on 24 July 2026, adding a further charge in Chapter 99. The practical effect is that the effective duty on Chinese-origin plastic tableware is now materially higher than the headline base rate most suppliers quote.

Why classification changes the total

Heading 3924 splits between 3924.10, which covers tableware and kitchenware such as cups, plates and cutlery, and 3924.90, the residual break for other household articles. Both carry a 3.4% base rate, but they have been administered under different Section 301 lists, and that difference is what drives the total.

The lesson for buyers is not to shop for a friendlier code — it is to make sure the code is right, and to ask your supplier for the product information your customs broker needs to classify it correctly. Material composition, intended use, whether an item is tableware or a household article, and whether the product incorporates an electrical component all affect the analysis. Get the classification right before you agree a landed cost, not after.

The category that escapes the worst of it

This is the most under-used lever in the whole discussion. Items classified as electrical goods rather than plastic tableware — rechargeable wine openers, electric salt and pepper grinders, milk frothers, coffee grinders — sit in a materially different duty position from a polystyrene wine glass. They also carry far higher unit values, which means the same container generates significantly more revenue per unit of duty paid.

For a US importer building an assortment in 2026, the sensible structure is to lead with the electrics for margin and use moulded drinkware for volume and repeat orders, rather than trying to compete on a container of commodity cups.

Two fees you can actually reduce

The merchandise processing fee is charged per formal entry, with a minimum and a maximum set annually, and the harbour maintenance fee applies to ocean cargo as a percentage of value. Neither is a tariff, and both are per-shipment charges rather than per-unit ones.

That makes consolidation a genuine cost lever. Three suppliers shipping to you separately means three entries and three processing fee minimums. One supplier consolidating the same goods into one shipment means one entry and one fee — and usually a better freight rate, because a full cube loads more efficiently than three partial ones. When you compare a factory-direct quote against a domestic distributor, put the fee structure next to the unit price; on mixed orders it is not a rounding error.

How to build a landed cost you can trust

Duty, taxes and clearance are the responsibility of the importer of record, and we are not a customs advisory service — confirm your position with your broker. What we can do is supply the documentation and product data your broker needs to classify the goods correctly, and ship consolidated so you pay one entry instead of three.

  • Get the correct HTS classification in writing from a licensed broker before you commit to a retail price
  • Ask the supplier for material composition, intended use and whether the item contains electronics
  • Confirm whether the product is a set or a single article, since sets are classified differently
  • Add the merchandise processing fee and harbour maintenance fee as separate lines, not a percentage of goods
  • Ask whether the supplier can consolidate multiple categories into one shipment and one entry
  • Re-check the Chapter 99 position before every large order, because scope and exclusions change

Questions on this topic

What is the duty rate on plastic drinkware from China?

The base MFN rate for plastic tableware under HTS heading 3924 is 3.4%, but Section 301 trade-action layers and an additional forced-labour action effective July 2026 are added on top in Chapter 99. The effective rate is therefore materially higher than the base rate. Confirm the current position with your customs broker before committing to a landed cost.

Which is cheaper to import, drinkware or kitchen electrics?

Per unit of value, kitchen electrics such as rechargeable grinders, frothers and wine openers sit in a materially better duty band than plastic tableware under heading 3924, and they carry much higher unit values. Many importers use electrics for margin and moulded drinkware for volume.

Can you reduce my fees?

We cannot change duty rates, but consolidating multiple categories into one shipment means one customs entry instead of several, which reduces per-shipment processing fees and usually improves the freight rate.

Do you provide documentation for customs?

Yes. We supply material composition, intended use, carton and weight data, and material certificates so your broker can classify the goods correctly. Duty and clearance remain the importer's responsibility.

What product data do you provide for customs classification?

We provide the model, the material, the capacity, the unit weight, the case pack and the carton dimensions per SKU, which is the data a broker needs to classify the goods. Import duty, taxes and clearance are the responsibility of the importer of record.

Request a quote

Do the delivery terms change the duty position?

The delivery term changes who arranges and pays the freight and the clearance, not the duty rate that applies to the goods. Confirm the term you want in the quotation request so the pricing basis is stated clearly.

Wholesale programme

Can electrical products and drinkware ship together?

They are quoted together and consolidated for shipment, but they are classified separately, so the classification data is provided per SKU rather than per shipment.
